questions.q: The orbit is described as a ___ surrounding the eye.
questions.exp: Bony cage surrounding eye. (Book p209)

questions.q: Match orbital wall with constituent bones — 1) Roof  2) Lateral wall  3) Floor … A) Maxilla, Zygomatic, Palatine  B) Frontal, Lesser wing of sphenoid  C) Zygomatic, Greater wing of sphenoid
questions.exp: Table: Roof Frontal + Lesser wing sphenoid; Lateral Zygomatic + Greater wing sphenoid; Floor Maxilla + Zygomatic + Palatine (m/c to fracture -> Blow out fracture). (Book p209)

questions.q: Which wall of orbit is most common to fracture, resulting in Blow out fracture?
questions.exp: Floor (m/c to fracture -> Blow out fracture). (Book p209)

questions.q: The thinnest wall of orbit is the medial wall, also called ___.
questions.exp: Medial wall -> Thinnest wall (Lamina papyracea). (Book p209)

questions.q: Bones forming the medial wall (mnemonic SMEL) are:
opts: Sphenoid body, Maxilla frontal process, Ethmoid bone, Lacrimal bone
questions.exp: Medial wall mnemonic SMEL : Sphenoid Body, Maxilla Frontal process, Ethmoid bone, Lacrimal bone. (Book p209)

questions.q: In the schematic orbit diagram, medial walls are parallel to each other separating orbit from nasal cavities (~2.5 cm apart), lateral walls are at 90° to each other separating orbit from middle cranial fossa, apex angle is 90° and each medial-lateral angle is:
questions.exp: Orbit : Schematic shows Medial walls Parallel 2.5 cm apart; Lateral walls 90° to each other; Apex 90°; 45° between medial and lateral at base. (Book p209)

questions.q: The Annulus of Zinn contains origin of all extra-ocular muscles EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Contains Annulus of Zinn -> Origin of all extra-ocular muscles (except Inferior Oblique). (Book p209)

questions.q: Openings into orbital apex are:
opts: Optic canal only without any fissures
Superior orbital fissure only on lateral wall
Optic canal + Superior fissure (roof-lateral) + Inferior fissure (floor-lateral)
Foramen rotundum and ovale of sphenoid bone
questions.exp: OPENINGS INTO ORBITAL APEX a Optic canal b Superior orbital fissure (Between roof and lateral wall) c Inferior orbital fissure (Between floor and lateral wall). (Book p209)

questions.q: In the 'Structures passing through the openings' diagram, which structures pass through the Annulus of Zinn?
opts: Only the optic nerve and central retinal artery
Optic nerve II, Ophthalmic artery, III superior/inferior, V1 nasociliary, VI abducent
Only the lacrimal nerve and frontal nerve
Only the trochlear nerve IV and lymphatics
questions.exp: Diagram shows Structures passing through Annulus of Zinn : Optic nerve CN II, Ophthalmic artery, Superior branch oculomotor III, Nasociliary V1, Abducent VI, Inferior branch oculomotor III, plus nearby Levator palpebrae, Superior oblique outside but near, lacrimal/frontal/trochlear outside. Also Superior ophthalmic vein, Inferior ophthalmic vein. (Book p209)

questions.q: The diagram of bones forming orbit labels all EXCEPT:
opts: Frontal bone, Supraorbital foramen, Nasal bone, Lacrimal bone, Ethmoid bone
Sphenoid bone, Superior orbital fissure, Optic canal, Zygomatic bone, Maxilla
Lacrimal fossa, Palatine bone, Infraorbital foramen
questions.exp: Bones forming orbit labels: Frontal, Supraorbital margin/foramen, Nasal, Sphenoid, Superior orbital fissure, Optic canal, Zygomatic, Maxilla, Lacrimal, Ethmoid, Lacrimal fossa, Palatine, Infraorbital foramen. (Book p209)

questions.q: Proptosis/Exophthalmos is defined as protrusion of eyeball from lateral orbital rim > ___ mm OR ___ mm difference between 2 eyes.
questions.exp: Protrusion >21mm OR 2mm difference between 2 eyes (as in text diagram). Note earlier line says >21mm. (Book p210)

questions.q: Match exophthalmometer — 1) Hertel's  2) Leude's … A) Only measures 1 eye at a time, Preferred in children  B) Can measure both eyes together, Preferred overall
questions.exp: Hertel's Can measure both eyes together Preferred overall; Leude's Only measures 1 eye at a time Preferred in children. Distance measured between Anterior part of cornea and Lateral orbital rim. (Book p210)

questions.q: Bilateral painless causes of proptosis listed include:
opts: Grave's disease, Cortico-cavernous fistula, Leukemia/AML (in children)
questions.exp: CAUSES Bilateral Painless : Grave's disease, Cortico-cavernous fistula, Leukemia/AML (in children); Painful : Cavernous sinus thrombosis, Grave's (restriction causing pain). (Book p210)

questions.q: Bilateral painful causes of proptosis listed are:
opts: Cavernous sinus thrombosis + Grave's with restrictive painful motility
Only orbital cellulitis unilaterally (not bilateral painful)
Only ON glioma and hemangioma (painless axial)
questions.exp: Bilateral Painful : Cavernous sinus thrombosis (CST), Grave's (restriction). (Book p210)

questions.q: Axial proptosis is along the 1° axis with outward, straight protrusion, whereas abaxial is ___ 1° axis and direction depends on cause.
questions.exp: Axial : Along 1° axis Outward straight protrusion; Abaxial : Away from 1° axis Direction depends on cause. (Book p210)

questions.q: Unilateral Axial proptosis — 1) Painful  2) Painless … A) ON glioma, Cavernous hemangioma  B) Orbital cellulitis, CST
questions.exp: Axial Painful : Orbital cellulitis, CST; Painless : ON glioma, Cavernous hemangioma. (Book p210)

questions.q: Unilateral Abaxial proptosis — Inferomedial, Upward, Lateral correspond to which causes? Inferomedial = Superotemporal lesions / Lacrimal gland tumors / Dermoid cysts; Upward = Maxillary sinus tumor; Lateral = Lacrimal sac ??? Check the table.
opts: Inferomedial: Superotemporal lesions/Lacrimal gland/Dermoid; Upward: maxillary sinus tumor; Lateral: Lacrimal sac lesion
questions.exp: Abaxial : Inferomedial : Superotemporal lesions, Lacrimal gland tumors, Dermoid cysts; Upward : maxillary sinus tumor; Lateral : Lacrimal sac ??? (as printed). (Book p210)

questions.q: Most common cause of proptosis — In adults is Grave's disease (unilateral or bilateral), In children U/L orbital cellulitis, B/L Leukemia/AML. True or false?
opts: False – adults most common is cellulitis
False – children most common is Grave's
questions.exp: m/c causes : In adults : Grave's disease. (Unilateral or bilateral proptosis.) In children : a U/L Orbital cellulitis, b B/L Leukemia/AML. (Book p211)

questions.q: Cavernous sinus thrombosis vs Orbital apex syndrome — Structures involved:
opts: CST: CN III,IV,VI,V1,Va ; OAS: CN II,III,IV,VI,V1 via fissure + optic canal
CST: Only CN II ; OAS: Only CN V2/V3
CST and OAS both involve only CN VII
CST: All cranial nerves II-XII equally
questions.exp: Table: Structures involved CST CN III,IV,VI,V1,Va ; OAS Contains structures passing through superior orbital fissure & optic canal CN II,III,IV,VI,V1. (Book p211)

questions.q: Ophthalmoplegia : Sequential vs Concurrent — CST shows Sequential CN VI -> III -> IV; OAS shows:
opts: Sequential CN III -> VI -> IV in reverse order
Concurrent: all nerves together -> all muscle actions lost simultaneously
Only CN VI palsy with no other involvement
Only isolated CN III palsy with sparing
questions.exp: CST : Sequential CN VI affected -> CN III -> CN IV; OAS : Concurrent ophthalmoplegia All nerves affected together -> All muscle actions lost at same time. Ophthalmic nerve V1 corneal anaesthesia Present in both. (Book p211)

questions.q: Visual loss D/t CN II palsy — CST vs OAS : CST No loss initially, Can be affected in late stages; OAS ___
questions.exp: Visual loss : CST No loss initially Can be affected late; OAS Complete LOV. (Book p211)

questions.q: Edema in mastoid area D/t CN V2? Actually table says D/t ??? – Present in CST, Absent in OAS. And Chemosis & Proptosis — CST B/L marked severe presenting feature, OAS U/L mild. True?
questions.exp: Second table: Visual loss as above; Edema in mastoid area D/t ??? Present in CST Absent in OAS; Chemosis & Proptosis CST B/L marked severe OAS U/L mild; Systemic signs marked vs mild; Presentation Always B/L (starts U/L) vs Always U/L. (Book p211)

questions.q: Cavernous sinus thrombosis always presents as B/L (starts U/L) while orbital apex syndrome always presents as ___ .
questions.exp: Presentation CST Always B/L (starts U/L); OAS Always U/L. (Book p211)

questions.q: Most common cause of orbital cellulitis is:
opts: Primary hematogenous spread from distant focus alone
Extension of paranasal sinusitis (Ethmoid sinusitis most common)
Exogenous trauma only without sinus involvement
questions.exp: ORBITAL CELLULITIS Causes : 1) Extension of paranasal sinusitis (m/c) : Ethmoid sinusitis (m/c). Staphylococcus and Streptococci m/c etiological agents. m/c in children with URTI. (Book p212)

questions.q: Most common etiological agents for orbital cellulitis are:
questions.exp: Staphylococcus and Streptococci : m/c etiological agents. (Book p212)

questions.q: Progression if no treatment : Pre-septal cellulitis (Eyelid edema Pain Inability to open eye Rx Topical/oral antibiotics) -> Orbital cellulitis (Proptosis Limitation of eye movement Rx IV antibiotics) -> ___ if still no Rx.
questions.exp: Progression : Pre-septal cellulitis If no Rx -> Orbital cellulitis If no Rx -> Subperiosteal abscess. Complications : Compression of optic nerve -> Blindness. (Book p212)

questions.q: Orbital septum is formed by and separates:
opts: Muscles/fascia/canthal ligaments; separates orbit into pre-septal and post-septal
Bone only forming the orbital walls separating sinuses
Conjunctiva only separating cornea from sclera
Nasal septum separating nasal cavities only
questions.exp: Note : Orbital septum Formed by muscles of eyelid, fascia, medial and lateral canthal ligament. Separates orbit from pre-orbital area forming Pre-septal Post-septal. (Book p212)

questions.q: Carotico-Cavernous Fistula (CCF) is an arterio-venous fistula between carotid artery & cavernous sinus. Cause in 75% cases is:
questions.exp: CCF Cause : Trauma (75% cases), Spontaneous. (Book p212)

questions.q: Features of CCF — Proptosis is:
opts: Unilateral non-pulsatile proptosis with no bruit or thrill
Bilateral pulsatile proptosis with bruit/thrill that stops with carotid pressure
Only upward displacement with no pulsatility
Only inferomedial displacement with chemosis only
questions.exp: Feature : Proptosis Bilateral Pulsatile Bruit & thrill present, stops on applying pressure to ipsilateral carotid artery. Ophthalmoplegia -> First affects CN VI. IOC Digital subtraction carotid angiography DSCA. (Book p212)

questions.q: In CCF, ophthalmoplegia first affects which cranial nerve?
questions.exp: Ophthalmoplegia -> First affects CN VI. (Book p212)

questions.q: Investigation of choice for CCF is:
opts: Non-contrast CT scan of brain only
questions.exp: IOC : Digital subtraction carotid angiography (DSCA). (Book p212)

questions.q: Orbital varices are defined as:
opts: Congenital enlargement of pre-existing venous channels
questions.exp: Orbital varices : Congenital enlargement of pre-existing venous channels. (Book p213)

questions.q: Features and complications of orbital varices — Proptosis Unilateral Bag of worms consistency on palpation Non-pulsatile No bruit no thrill Complication:
questions.exp: Features : Unilateral Bag of worms, Non-pulsatile No bruit no thrill. Complication : Orbital hemorrhage/thrombosis. (Book p213)

questions.q: Match intermittent proptosis trigger with cause — 1) ↑ on Valsalva/bending forward  2) ↑ with URTI  3) ↑ on crying … A) Orbital varices  B) Orbital lymphangiomas  C) Capillary hemangioma (children) / Encephalocele (infants)
questions.exp: Intermittent proptosis : ↑ on Valsalva/bending forward Orbital varices; ↑ with URTI Orbital lymphangiomas; ↑ on crying Children Capillary hemangioma Infants Encephalocele. Pulsatile: Cortico cavernous fistula, Orbital roof fracture in NF-1 / Trauma. (Book p213)

questions.q: Pulsatile proptosis causes include:
opts: Cortico-cavernous fistula or Orbital roof fracture in NF-1/Trauma
Capillary hemangioma only in infants (on crying)
questions.exp: Pulsatile proptosis : Cortico cavernous fistula, Orbital roof fracture in NF-1 / Trauma. (Book p213)

questions.q: Pseudo proptosis is appearance of eyeball protrusion. Causes include all EXCEPT:
opts: Retraction of upper eyelid (can be side effect of apraclonidine)
Enophthalmos where contralateral eye appears proptosed (Trauma, Horner's)
questions.exp: Pseudo proptosis Causes : Retraction of upper eyelid Can be side effect of apraclonidine; Enophthalmos Contralateral eye appears proptosed Seen in Trauma, Horner's; Axial length >26mm; Buphthalmos (enlarged eyeball). (Book p213)

questions.q: Thyroid Associated Ophthalmology (TAO) — Most common cause of unilateral and bilateral proptosis in adults, can occur in:
questions.exp: TAO OVERVIEW m/c cause of unilateral and bilateral proptosis in adults. Can occur in any state of thyroid activity. (Book p213)

questions.q: Pathogenesis of TAO includes:
opts: Only orbital fat atrophy with enophthalmos occurring
EOM enlargement + fat infiltration pushing eyeball forward to frank proptosis
Only muscle fibrosis without inflammatory swelling
Only lacrimal gland hypertrophy with tearing
questions.exp: Pathogenesis : Inflammation -> Enlargement of extra-ocular muscles. Inflammation and infiltration of orbital fat -> Pushing of eyeball forward -> Frank proptosis. (Book p213)

questions.q: Match TAO signs — 1) Goldzeiher's sign (earliest)  2) Dalyrymple sign (m/c)  3) Proptosis (2nd m/c) … A) Congestion/hyperemia  B) Upper eyelid retraction -> pseudo proptosis D/t constriction of Muller's muscle Seen in 93% C) Axial uni/bilateral Seen in 60%
questions.exp: Table : Goldzeiher's sign (earliest) Congestion/hyperemia; Dalyrymple sign (m/c) upper eyelid retraction -> pseudo proptosis D/t constriction of Muller's muscle Seen in 93%; Proptosis (2nd m/c) Axial uni/bilateral Seen in 60%. (Book p214)

questions.q: Von Graefe sign, Kocher's sign, Stellwags sign in TAO are:
opts: von Graefe lid lag on downgaze, Kocher staring/startled, Stellwag reduced blinking
All are pupillary light reflex abnormalities only
All are optic nerve head changes on disc exam
Only von Graefe is relevant, others are absent in TAO
questions.exp: Von Graefe sign Lid lag On downgaze upper eyelid does not move down; Kocher's sign Staring/startled appearance; Stellwags sign Reduced eyelid blinking d/t upper eyelid retraction. (Book p214)

questions.q: Restrictive squint in TAO is due to Fibrosis of extra ocular muscles -> Loss of movement; muscle affected first is:
questions.exp: Restrictive squint Fibrosis of extra ocular muscles -> Loss of movement muscle affected first : Inferior rectus. (Elevation affected first). (Book p214)

questions.q: Clinical photographs show Dalyrymple sign (upper eyelid retraction) and proptosis vs normal side, and Von Graefe sign showing eyeball down eyelid lagging. Which sign is marked as earliest?
questions.exp: Goldzeiher's sign (earliest) Congestion/hyperemia. Dalyrymple m/c, Proptosis 2nd m/c. (Book p214)

questions.q: Complication of TAO due to inability to close eye is:
opts: Primary cataract formation with lens opacity
Exposure keratitis from lagophthalmos and incomplete closure
Acute angle-closure glaucoma with rising IOP
questions.exp: Complication : Exposure Keratitis (EK) d/t inability to close eye. Management : Ensure euthyroid state. Supportive For EK Lubricants, For upper lid retraction Botox injection into Muller's muscle, For inflammation Systemic steroids. (Book p214)

questions.q: Management for TAO upper lid retraction and inflammation are:
opts: Upper lid retraction Botox injection into levator, inflammation topical antibiotics
Upper lid retraction Botox injection into Muller's muscle, For inflammation Systemic steroids, For EK Lubricants
questions.exp: For EK Lubricants; For upper lid retraction Botox injection into Muller's muscle; For inflammation Systemic steroids. (Book p214)
